I will not bore your listeners with the history of it. It dates back to World War I. It is an accident of history. A lot of people believe this fairy tale that the Founding Fathers, sitting in my district in Independence Hall, dreamt up the debt ceiling as this way to force Congress to deal with debt. So there actually is no mechanism by law that is supposed to force members of Congress to really think about issuing new debt. I would say the only thing that exists in that respect is the annual appropriations process. If people did believe, however, that the original idea behind the debt ceiling was to force Congress to deal with the debt issue, I would say that concept has failed miserably. So I have a reform to the debt ceiling, very simply what it says is it's basically what happened in 2011, and that took effect for two years, made permanent. What happened in 2011, and to resolve that debt ceiling in pass, was that the Treasury Secretary had the ability to initiate an increase in the debt ceiling. Congress had the ability to stop it if they voted to do so. But apps in any congressional action the debt ceiling would increase given the Treasury Secretary initiated it.
